mitre_assessments.name: JavaScript
mitre_assessments.rationale: The reviewed command line uses vbscript:Execute, and JavaScript is not observed in that command. The Sigma tag is retained for provenance but is not treated as supported by the current evidence.

mitre_assessments.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
mitre_assessments.rationale: The resolver only resolved a Sigma tag. The two reviewed evidence groups are insufficient to assess T1140, and the required full negative scan and broader evaluation have not been performed. This milestone therefore does not make a not_observed_in_reviewed_scope determination.

mitre_assessments.name: Mshta
mitre_assessments.rationale: mshta.exe is directly observed in the first evidence group, and its launch of PowerShell is directly observed in the second. This supports the candidate technique at the evidence level only and does not finalize the assessment.

scenario.description: Reviewable MSHTA-PowerShell scenario in which cmd.exe launches mshta.exe and mshta.exe launches powershell.exe with -noexit -command Get-Service sysmon. Process creation records establish the launch command, not successful cmdlet completion or a finalized attack determination.

sigma_findings.rule_title: MSHTA Execution with Suspicious File Extensions

limitations: This ground truth scope covers only the two reviewed behavior and evidence groups.
The two Sysmon observations carry upstream timestamp_conflict review issues.
A full-dataset negative scan has not been performed, so absence claims cannot be made across the full scope.
MITRE assessments remain candidates and require human review.
Process-creation telemetry does not establish successful cmdlet completion, output, or the Sysmon service state.
Canonical timestamps follow TimeCreated; Sysmon UtcTime differs by about four hours and its timezone is unresolved.

The file also contains conhost creation, event-log clearing and temporary-file deletion telemetry outside this two-group core. These must not be described as globally absent or automatically classified as a destructive payload.
CTI facts are publisher-reported external context. They do not establish local host compromise, campaign attribution, HTTP completion or confirmed C2.
Publisher excerpts, publisher paraphrases and project analyst comparisons have separate origins. Analyst interpretation is not a publisher quote or local observed evidence.
observed_behavior: cmd.exe launched mshta.exe with an inline vbscript:Execute command.
PowerShell was launched with -noexit -command Get-Service sysmon.
